findings.failureMode: An unrelated or fork origin can contain the same known parent SHA. Checking the intended GitHub main separately and only comparing ls-remote parent does not establish that the push target is the intended repository.
findings.counterexample: A repository with an origin pointing to another owner and the known docs parent would pass the former parent comparison while the separate gh main check addressed the intended repository. This was a source-path counterexample, not an executed Git mutation.
findings.smallestCorrection: Verify all origin fetch and push URLs against the exact intended repository before any object/index/ref/push write; avoid exposing rejected credential-bearing URLs.
findings.resolution: Exact allowlisted HTTPS/SSH origin fetch and push URLs are checked before read-tree/hash-object/commit-tree/update-ref/push. The rejection message contains no rejected URL. C read the actual effect routing; primary pure controls reject other owners, lookalike repositories/domains and file URLs.

findings.failureMode: The former final readback checked only issue body/state and the new comment. Main or complete discussion could change after publication without invalidating the claimed current publication result.
findings.counterexample: An intervening owner discussion addition or main change after the approved comment POST would have been absent from the previous final guard. This is an unexecuted source-path counterexample.
findings.smallestCorrection: Read back main, issue identity/body/title/state and the complete discussion; allow only the exact approved marker comment in addition to the frozen discussion.
findings.resolution: The actual post-effect path reads comment, issue, paginated discussion and main, then invokes poststate_errors. Drift records PUBLISHED_REQUIRES_RECONCILIATION, comment ID/URL and exact errors before raising. Primary pure controls discriminate main/body/state/new/deleted/edited discussion and duplicate-marker drift. The publisher has no issue-state mutation path.

findings.failureMode: A copied or stale receipt could be appended without first verifying that its stored effect identity matched the current issue approval.
findings.counterexample: A receipt copied from a different issue/revision/specification commit could retain incorrect identity fields while recording the new operation. No such actual external action was run in this review.
findings.smallestCorrection: Check number, canonical ID, revision, source target, specification commit and exact approved comment hash before appending any step.
findings.resolution: The receipt identity helper checks all six fields before the first record() call. Primary pure controls reject each changed field. Marker lookup precedes any retry POST, identical revisions are reused, divergent/duplicate revisions stop, and existing effect receipts are preserved.

findings.failureMode: Trusting exactFilesVerified as a historical flag without comparing the current source bytes could transform a changed comment and automatically mark its approval PASS under the old cold review.
findings.counterexample: Change any current spec/comment/metadata byte after reconciliation but before preparation. The former transformation path would read the changed bytes without comparing coldRead.reviewedFiles. The pre-correction helper/routing is retained in workers/C/package-review-final-v1; no external publication was attempted.
findings.smallestCorrection: Share an exact expected spec/comment/metadata path-set and byte-hash check, and call it before staging and per-issue preparation/approval.
findings.resolution: verify_reviewed_source checks the exact triple and all three SHA256 values; both stage and prepare call it before transforming source or approving a comment. C invoked the actual pure helper on all26 unchanged triples and observed expected rejection for each of the three drifted hashes and an incomplete triple. Source author files remain unchanged.
